prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological classification of insulators, and for its first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: Topological insulators are a clean, universal mechanism: bulk topology enforces protected edge states, with an invariant (Z2) that can be stated and analysed rigorously and that survives disorder. The prediction by Kane and Mele (with the Z2 classification) was followed by a decisive transport experiment by Molenkamp's group, so the theory-to-measurement chain is complete and has been reproduced across many platforms for roughly two decades. The concept has spread into photonics, cold atoms, acoustics and mechanical metamaterials, which is the cross-disciplinary reach I value. Of the shortlisted candidates it is the one where I can most confidently say that the essential mechanism is understood, not just that the device works.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang made the HgTe prediction that guided Molenkamp's experiment, Hasan's ARPES work on 3D topological insulators is arguably as decisive as the 2D branch, and Murakami and Fu-Kane-Mele also contributed, so any three names leave out people with a serious claim. There is also the question whether the 2016 prize for topological phases and phase transitions has already covered the conceptual core, and whether the committee would rather award a candidate with broader support such as optical lattice clocks, where the credit is clean (two names) and seven of eight members ranked it.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks twisted bilayer graphene first and topological insulators second, arguing that the flat-band prediction followed by experiment is the model theory-to-measurement link, and that the 2016 prize does not preclude a follow-on topological prize.
responses.response: I agree on the 2016 point: Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz were honoured for topological phase transitions and the integer quantum Hall lineage, and time-reversal-symmetric Z2 insulators are a distinct, protected-by-symmetry phenomenon. Where I differ is on maturity. In twisted bilayer graphene the discovery is secure but the pairing mechanism and the role of strain and disorder are still disputed, whereas for the quantum spin Hall edge the interpretation has been stable for two decades. I keep B051 as a strong alternative, but I would rather award the field whose mechanism is settled.

responses.point: Olsson includes Hasan with Kane and Molenkamp for topological insulators, arguing that the direct ARPES observation of spin-momentum-locked surface states is decisive and that Mele's contribution is hard to separate from Kane's.
responses.response: This is the serious disagreement within our own cluster and I take it seriously. Hasan's 3D observations are a distinct achievement. But Kane and Mele's 2005 papers introduced both the quantum spin Hall state and the Z2 invariant jointly, and the later 3D classification (Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents, Roy) builds on that structure, so removing Mele would break the theoretical attribution while omitting Hasan breaks the 3D experimental one. If the committee prefers Hasan, the only way to keep him is to drop a theorist or Molenkamp; I would resist dropping Mele, and I would phrase the citation around the 2D quantum spin Hall effect, which is what the supplied three names support most cleanly.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks optical lattice clocks first because Katori's magic-wavelength idea, made quantitative by accurate atomic structure theory, was then taken to the 1e-18 level by Ye's group, with a clean two-name credit and an approaching redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I ranked B010 only eighth, and your argument and Kroll's make me revise that: the attribution is cleaner than for any topological configuration and maturity is very high. My residual hesitation is conceptual rather than scientific. Clocks are a superb measurement achievement, but a large part of the credit for the enabling tools already went to the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. I regard B010 as a genuine alternative and would support it if the committee cannot agree on a fair topological allocation.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks IceCube neutrino astronomy first as a discovery found in nature that opened a new window, and also ranks topological insulators second, noting that the four-person allocation problem is the real difficulty.
responses.response: I share your concern about the four-way allocation and think we should state openly that a three-name topological prize is a compromise. On IceCube, I cannot assess the detector and analysis details, and the large-collaboration problem is as severe as for the Higgs: Halzen, Karle and Spiering are central, but the choice among the founding group is partly subjective, and source identification (NGC 1068, TXS 0506+056) is still thin. Compared with that, the quantum spin Hall effect has a more compact attribution.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts Kane, Mele and Molenkamp without Hasan, and without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, as a fair allocation.
Whether the 2016 topological-phase prize makes a second topological prize look redundant.
Whether the broader support for optical lattice clocks should outweigh my own conceptual preference.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I am in the same Gothenburg physics environment as Goran Johansson and Eva Olsson at Chalmers, but no specific collaboration with any shortlisted candidate is known.
